title: Students in Berlin and across Germany plan protests against austerity and schools

tea.why: Students and youth are protesting broken schools, austerity, the cost of living, social injustice, military conscription and climate change.
tea.want: Demonstrators demand action regarding broken schools, living costs, social injustice, military conscription and climate concerns.
tea.changed: Oct 21: A youth initiative announced plans for mass demonstrations across 21 German cities, including Berlin, for October 31.

summary: A youth initiative named Gen Z regelt has called for mass protests across twenty-one cities in Germany, including Berlin, Cologne, Hamburg, and Munich. Thousands of participants are expected to take part in demonstrations addressing broken schools, government austerity, rising living costs, social injustice, military conscription, and climate change. Organisers have stated that the initiative is strictly against all forms of violence directed at people or property. Meanwhile, police authorities have stated they are vigilant and prepared to protect the right to congregate, though union officials warned that law enforcement will respond firmly to any potential disruptions or attempts by radicals to hijack the demonstrations.
response: Police stated they are vigilant and relaxed while intending to protect the right to congregate, though the head of the Federal Police's GdP union warned that state and federal officers will offer a firm response to any trouble or destructive behavior.

updates.text: The youth initiative Gen Z regelt announced plans for mass protests in 21 German cities scheduled for October 31.
